code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: pv-azuredisk-manual
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 10Gi
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  azureDisk:
    diskName: myAKSDisk
    diskURI: /subscriptions/xxxx/.../disks/myAKSDisk
    kind: Managed
caption: A PV exists independently of any Pod — it just declares a disk is available.

eyebrow: A PersistentVolumeClaim: the request that gets matched
code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: pvc-azuredisk
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 10Gi

# kubectl get pvc pvc-azuredisk
# STATUS   Bound   -> matched to a PV
caption: The control plane binds a PVC to a compatible PV — size, accessMode, both must fit.

steps.label: ReadWriteOnce (RWO)
steps.sub: one node mounts read-write — Azure Disk, AWS EBS

steps.label: ReadOnlyMany (ROX)
steps.sub: many nodes mount read-only at once

steps.label: ReadWriteMany (RWX)
steps.sub: many nodes read-write — needs Azure Files or NFS, not a disk

eyebrow: Mounting the claim in a Pod
code:
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: myregistry.azurecr.io/myapp:1.4
      volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /data
          name: data-volume
  volumes:
    - name: data-volume
      persistentVolumeClaim:
        claimName: pvc-azuredisk
caption: The Pod references the PVC by name — never the PV, never the disk directly.

subtitle: Letting the cloud create the disk on demand, instead of by hand.
